questions.question: What is the highest mountain on the Australian mainland?
questions.explanation: Kosciuszko, in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales, is 2,228 metres high. Mount Townsend, its neighbour, is second.

questions.question: In which event did Cathy Freeman win gold at the Sydney 2000 Olympics?
questions.explanation: Freeman, who had lit the cauldron ten days earlier, won in 49.11 seconds in front of more than 110,000 people.

questions.question: In which year did Australians vote in a referendum to count Aboriginal people in the census and allow the Commonwealth to make laws for them?
questions.explanation: More than 90 per cent of voters said yes on 27 May 1967, the highest yes vote in any Australian referendum.
questions.source: National Museum of Australia, Defining Moments

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets combined.

questions.question: Who wrote the 1991 novel Cloudstreet?
questions.explanation: Cloudstreet follows two families sharing a large house in Perth over twenty years. It won the Miles Franklin Award in 1992.

questions.question: Which country has the largest population in the world?
questions.explanation: The United Nations estimates that India passed China in 2023. Each has more than 1.4 billion people.

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which state?
questions.explanation: The reef stretches about 2,300 kilometres along the Queensland coast. Western Australia has a major reef of its own, Ningaloo.
questions.source: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: Leonardo began the portrait in Florence around 1503. It hangs in the Louvre, where it was stolen in 1911 and missing for more than two years.

questions.question: Which Australian marsupial produces cube-shaped droppings?
questions.explanation: The shape forms in the last section of the wombat's intestine, where the walls vary in stiffness. Researchers who worked this out won an Ig Nobel Prize in 2019.

questions.question: In which year did humans first walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed in July 1969. Television pictures of the moonwalk reached the world through tracking stations at Honeysuckle Creek near Canberra and Parkes in New South Wales.
